The two inositol-phosphate ligands contact it directly: 4IP in 1BWN at 2.75 \u00c5 (4 of 6 4IP instances contact residue 28) and 4PT in 2Z0P at 2.58 \u00c5 (4 of 4 instances). Negative-control ligands (3IS, 72V, A1JS1, IS7, MG, NYQ, Q1B, ZN) never contact residue 28. The refuting criterion (ligand-bound structures show R28 outside contact distance) was not met. The test does not measure binding free energy, so the second refuting clause (\u0394\u0394G < 0.5 kcal/mol) is still open."}, {"id": "H2", "verdict": "unchanged", "why": "T1 measures ligand proximity only. It does not measure PH-TH or homodimer interface burial, so it does not bear on H2's refuting criterion (interface burial and interface contact energy). Contacts with the synthetic benzofuran ligands are not evidence about dimerisation."}, {"id": "H3", "verdict": "unchanged", "why": "T1 gives no folding free energy, buried-bond or \u0394\u0394G value, so it does not bear on H3's refuting criterion (predicted \u0394\u0394G near zero or stabilising). The R28C structures show 0 ligand contacts, but those structures bind only ZN, MG or 72V/3IS, so this reflects the absence of an inositol-type ligand, not fold stability."}], "uncertainty": "The test is a crystal-contact check, not a binding measurement. The structures use soluble analogues and wild-type or other-mutant proteins, not R28H. Most of the 32 contacts come from the synthetic benzofuran ligand series (A1B6*, A1JS*, etc.), so a contact at R28 shows the residue sits in a ligand-accessible environment in general. Only 4IP and 4PT are inositol-phosphate-like and are the ligands H1 names. Absence of contact in the R28C structures reflects missing ligands there, not a loss of binding. The H1 result needs a computed or measured \u0394\u0394G of binding for R28H versus wild type with Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 or the 4IP/4PT analogue, and the R28C control, before H1 is considered confirmed."}
